title: How the NAIST Muslim Community Scheduler works
intro: The NAIST Muslim Community Scheduler plans the community's schedules: the Friday prayer (Jumat) khatib and imam, and Isha + Tarawih with the kultum in Ramadan. Flowcharts of the whole system: what a member sees, what the admin does, what runs by itself, and what to do when the admin changes. This page is part of the website and is updated whenever the system changes.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.blurb: Everything in one view, and what a normal week looks like.

diagrams.title: The system: people, website, robot and messages
diagrams.caption: Members, scheduled people and the admin all use the same web page. The robot sends the reminders and keeps things in step; the admin posts the announcement in the WhatsApp and Facebook groups by hand.

diagrams.title: A normal week
diagrams.caption: From the first availability mark to the prayer on Friday. Times are Japan time.

sections.blurb: What anyone can do without a password, and what happens to someone who is scheduled.

diagrams.title: What you can do on the website
diagrams.caption: No password is needed to look at the schedule, to share the announcement, to add the calendar or to say when you can come.

diagrams.title: If you are scheduled as khatib or imam

sections.title: For the admin
sections.blurb: The weekly routine, how to set up the people, and what to do when someone cannot come.

diagrams.title: The weekly routine
diagrams.caption: Most of it is picking people. The robot sends the reminders; you only send by hand to people the robot cannot reach, and post the announcement in the groups.

diagrams.title: The roster: people and how to reach them
diagrams.caption: The more ways a person can be reached, the less you do by hand.

diagrams.title: When someone cannot find their name
diagrams.caption: They send their details; you are told and add them with one click.

diagrams.title: When someone cannot make it
diagrams.caption: The alert reaches you on the website and by email, so a replacement can be found early.

diagrams.title: Ramadan: Isha + Tarawih and the kultum
diagrams.caption: Set the dates and the weekly pattern once; the days are made for you and each can be adjusted.

sections.title: Behind the scenes
sections.blurb: What runs by itself, and the exact list of pages, tables, jobs and settings in the code (this list is written by the code itself, so it is always current).

diagrams.title: What runs when
diagrams.caption: Three triggers: an edit on the website, the twice-daily job, and a change of the code.

sections.title: When the admin changes
sections.blurb: Three levels, from the everyday handover to moving the whole system.

diagrams.title: 1. Hand over the admin job (about 5 minutes)
diagrams.caption: The everyday case: another person takes over the weekly work.

diagrams.title: 2. If the old admin leaves: change the keys they knew
diagrams.caption: Each key is separate. Change only the ones that person had. Never send a key or password in a chat; give it in a private message or a password manager.

diagrams.title: 3. Moving everything to the new owner's own accounts (rare)
diagrams.caption: Not rehearsed yet: treat it as a checklist and ask a developer for steps 4 and 6.

sections.title: Setup and what is switched on
sections.blurb: The optional parts, which ones are done, and the steps for the Google Calendar connection.

diagrams.title: Connecting Google Calendar (about 15 minutes, once)
diagrams.caption: Needs the community Gmail account (it stays when admins change) and a computer. Full wording is in the README, section Google Calendar.

features.name: My name isn't listed
features.what: Someone not on the roster types their name and details; the admin is told and adds them. Nothing is added automatically.

features.name: See the schedule
features.what: A calendar of the Fridays with khatib, imam and venue.

features.name: Friday details and announcement
features.what: Tap a Friday to read it and copy the weekly announcement.

features.name: Name locked on the device
features.what: After a member picks their name under You are, it cannot be changed on that device (so nobody marks or looks at someone else's availability). A person can use several devices: each one is remembered by the website, and the admin sees them under Edit person (with the device type and when it was last opened) and can reset one or all, after which that device can choose a name again the next time it opens the page. The admin can also tick Shared device on a device (with the access code entered): that device is never locked, so many people can choose their name on it. It is a guard in the page, not a login.

features.name: Say when you can or cannot come
features.what: Choose your name, then I'm available or I'm unavailable. No password.

features.name: Can't make it link
features.what: In every reminder and calendar event: one button that tells the admin you cannot come.

features.name: Calendar feed
features.what: A feed for Apple, Outlook or Google (From URL): 12:35 to 13:05 each Friday with the announcement text.

features.name: Public Google Calendar
features.what: A shared Google Calendar the website keeps up to date within a minute.

features.name: Reminder emails
features.what: 7 days before and the day before, to people whose email is on the roster.

features.name: Reminder LINE messages
features.what: The same reminders on LINE, for people who linked the bot.

features.name: Khutbah checklist for the khatib
features.what: A khatib's reminders (email, LINE, and the Copy / WhatsApp text) carry the five rukun of the Friday khutbah in the Shafi'i madzhab: hamdalah, shalawat on the Prophet and wasiat taqwa in both khutbahs, a verse of the Qur'an in one of them, and du'a for the believers in the second; plus the main conditions (the rukun in Arabic, standing, sitting briefly between the two khutbahs, wudu, audible, within Zuhr time, no long break). A tick on each person in the roster (on by default) turns it off for someone who does not need it.

features.name: Add to Google Calendar link
features.what: In every reminder: a ready-made calendar event with their role.

features.name: Google Calendar invitation
features.what: Invited automatically, at the email on the roster (or a separate Google Calendar address if one is saved), unless reminders are off.

features.name: Access code
features.what: Unlocks editing. Members never need it.

features.name: Roster
features.what: Add, edit, mark left NAIST or delete people; their contact details are visible only with the code.

features.name: Planner
features.what: Pick primary khatib, secondary khatib and imam for every coming Friday, with availability and turns shown. The secondary (standby, usually next week's khatib) gets no automatic reminder or invitation.

features.name: Guest speaker
features.what: Type a name such as Prof. Arai under any slot for someone who is not in the roster. They show in the calendar, announcement and Google event; no reminders can be sent to them, so the admin to-do lists them to message by hand.

features.name: Copy reminder and WhatsApp buttons
features.what: For people the robot cannot reach: copy the text or open WhatsApp with it typed.

features.name: Announcement for the groups
features.what: Generate and copy the weekly announcement to post in the WhatsApp and Facebook groups.

features.name: Admin to-do messages
features.what: A week before (only if something needs doing) and the day before: who to message by hand, empty slots, post the announcement.

features.name: Can't-make-it alerts
features.what: A red box and badge in the planner, and an email, when a scheduled person cannot come.

features.name: Invitation test mode
features.what: In the planner: invite only one address (your own) until you turn it off, to try the Google invitations before anyone else gets one.

features.name: Google Calendar sync
features.what: Status line and a Sync now button in the planner; instant alert emails.

features.name: Daily job
features.what: 08:23 and 14:23 Japan time: reminders, to-dos, alert emails, calendar re-sync.

features.name: Deploy
features.what: Every change of the code is published automatically, with its database changes.

features.name: Join requests
features.what: A box in the planner lists people who could not find their name, with Add to roster (form pre-filled) and Dismiss; the admins are also emailed.

features.name: Places
features.what: A card in the planner to add, edit and delete places (dorm lounges, the Sentan assembly room) with details and a map link (or tick TOA rooms from a list to add them as places already linked to their room, with the map link taken from the room's location in TOA); the Friday venue becomes a dropdown, and the details and link go into the announcement and the calendar event.

features.name: Ramadan days
features.what: First and last day of Ramadan, a weekly pattern (which weekdays, which place, what time, kultum or not) and one editable day each, with the kultum speaker (roster or guest) and an announcement. The kultum speaker is reminded by email or LINE 3, 2 and 1 day before and on the day (a guest is not), and each evening appears in Google Calendar and the public calendar feed with the speaker invited.

features.name: Ramadan days in the calendar
features.what: Isha + Tarawih days show as a moon chip with the time (and a microphone when there is a kultum); tap one for the place, time, speaker and the announcement.

features.name: Ramadan evenings in the TOA app
features.what: Pick a place's TOA room by name on the Places card (the list is every TOA room the integration key's owner administers, refreshed by the daily job; no long ids to type). The daily job (or the toa_check option in Actions) then adds each Isha + Tarawih evening held there to that room's TOA queue through TOA's own API, with the kultum speaker, changes it when the day changes and removes it when the day is deleted, without notifying the people nearby for every evening. It needs the TOA integration key; until then nothing is sent to TOA.

features.name: Link to the TOA app
features.what: When a place is linked to its TOA room, its announcement (Fridays and Ramadan evenings), the Google Calendar and calendar-feed event and the day's window carry a link to that room in the TOA web app, where the queue and any live broadcast can be followed.

features.name: TOA bookings for book-only rooms
features.what: For a place linked to a TOA room that is open only when booked, every Friday prayer and Ramadan evening held there becomes a TOA booking at exactly the scheduled time (Friday 12:35 for 30 minutes; the evening's start for its length). The daily job (or toa_check in Actions) adds, moves and removes them with the schedule. A hand-made booking is kept; a hand-started toa_check with toa_replace_bookings also replaces a one-off hand-made booking that overlaps a scheduled prayer.

setup.name: Community access code
setup.detail: Set. Change it with the handover chart if an admin leaves.

setup.name: Reminder emails (community Gmail)
setup.detail: Test email received. Add each person's email in the roster to start their reminders.

setup.name: LINE reminders
setup.detail: Bot connected. Each person links with a code from the roster.

setup.name: Google Calendar connection
setup.detail: Connected and checked: the Google script answered and the Fridays were written to the NAIST Jumat calendar. Last step of the chart: look at the public calendar in a private window.

setup.name: An admin marked in the roster
setup.detail: Edit your own entry and tick Admin this period (needs an email or LINE link).

setup.name: TOA integration key
setup.detail: TOA now has its own API for schedulers. In the TOA app go to Settings, Integration keys, New key (name it NAIST scheduler), copy the key once into the GitHub secret TOA_API_KEY, then run Actions: Send Jumat reminders with toa_check. The old TOA_EMAIL and TOA_PASSWORD secrets are no longer used and can be deleted.

setup.name: GitHub default branch set to main
setup.detail: main is the default branch, so new pull requests and the schedule use it.
